prerequisites: Familiarity with fundamental calculus and mathematics
Basic first-year subjects that contain or use physical and mathematical concepts

learning_outcomes.text: Understand and possess knowledge.
Application of knowledge.
Ability to make judgments.
Ability to communicate and social aptitude.
Ability to learn.
Ability to learn to work autonomously.
Ability to solve problems.
Social competence and global citizenship.
Basic knowledge of the profession.
Skill in the use of ICT.
Knowledge and abilities to apply the fundamentals of elasticity and material resistance to the behavior of real solids.
Knowledge and ability for the calculation and design of industrial structures and constructions.
Provide adequate training in the theoretical and technological bases proper to Industrial Technical Engineering.
Provide adequate training in the drafting of construction, demolition, manufacturing, installation, assembly or operation projects of movable or immovable property specific to the specialty.
Provide adequate training in the execution of measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert opinions, studies, reports, etc., and in industrial management.
Understand the basic concepts and general principles of construction.
Have full knowledge of the behavior of both metallic and concrete structures when designing and calculating an industrial construction.
Achieve student involvement in teaching activity through works that develop their creativity, also fostering their capacity for analysis, synthesis, and management of all available information.
Ensure that the student is capable of autonomous work and learning, fostering the use of different bibliographic sources.
Exercises will be proposed so that the student is able to apply theoretical concepts to practical cases.
Problem-based learning (PBL) and other types of activities will be carried out, whose initiative is to prevent the student from being a mere passive agent.
Practical classes will aim to enable students to put into practice the knowledge acquired in theoretical classes.

Be able to apply current regulations and the technical building code to situations posed in practical cases that respond to market demand and the stated need of each sector for the construction of industrial structures.
Study and apply the concepts of calculation and design of industrial structures and constructions.
Become proficient in the field of engineering.

syllabus_topics: Block 1: Bases for Steel Structure Calculation according to CTE
Topic 2. Main parts of an industrial building.
Topic 4: Sizing of supports or columns.
Topic 7. Bases for Limit State calculation.
Topic 8. Ultimate limit state under design loads.
Topic 10. Concepts and types of foundation.
Topic 12. Geotechnical soil study. Settlements in foundations.
assessment_rules: For the Ordinary Call, the final grade is composed of 20% from evaluated activities and 80% from a final exam. If students do not submit activities, the final exam will account for 100% of their grade. For the Extraordinary Call, students can choose a final exam accounting for 80% (if activities were submitted) or 100% of the grade. For students eligible for a Unique Final Evaluation, a single exam will assess 100% of the course competencies and constitute 100% of the final grade. Artificial Intelligence will not be used in the assessment system.
